title: Practical Skills Academy
description: Real-life skills for everyday independence, safety, and wellbeing — progressing from beginner to advanced.

skills.title: Wash Hands Before Cooking
skills.description: Always wash hands with soap and water for 20 seconds before touching food.
skills.why: Prevents germs from spreading to food and people.

skills.title: Make a Simple Sandwich
skills.description: Spread butter on two bread slices. Add filling (cheese, jam, or salad). Press together and cut diagonally.
skills.why: Independence skill — being able to prepare your own snack.

skills.title: Pour a Safe Drink
skills.description: Use both hands to hold a jug or bottle. Pour slowly over the sink first to practise control.

quiz.question: How long should you wash your hands before cooking?
What is the safest way to hold a knife when cutting?
options: With a 'claw' grip on the food

skills.title: Boil Pasta Safely
skills.description: Fill pot with water, add salt, bring to boil. Add pasta, stir. Cook per packet instructions. Drain carefully with adult supervision for hot water.
skills.why: Core cooking skill; teaches heat safety.

skills.title: Scrambled Eggs
skills.description: Crack 2 eggs into a bowl, beat with fork. Add pinch of salt. Cook in buttered pan on medium heat, stirring gently until just set.

skills.title: Read and Follow a Recipe
skills.description: Gather all ingredients first (mise en place). Read all steps before starting. Measure accurately. Follow steps in order.
skills.why: Planning and literacy skills applied to cooking.

quiz.question: What does 'mise en place' mean?
options: Everything in its place — ingredients prepared before cooking

quiz.question: Why do we add salt to pasta water?
options: For flavour and to season the pasta

skills.title: Plan a Weekly Menu
skills.description: Plan 7 dinners considering nutrition (proteins, vegetables, carbs), budget, and variety. Write a shopping list organised by supermarket section.

skills.title: Safe Knife Skills
skills.description: Learn the claw grip, bridge grip, and rocking motion. Keep knives sharp — dull knives slip. Always cut away from your body.
skills.why: Safety and efficiency in the kitchen.

skills.title: Bake a Simple Loaf
skills.description: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast, 1 tsp salt, 300ml warm water. Knead 10 min, rest 1 hour, shape, prove 30 min, bake 200°C for 30 min.
skills.why: Teaches chemistry of yeast, patience, and planning.

quiz.question: What is the correct internal temperature for cooked chicken?
What does 'sauté' mean?
options: Cook in a small amount of oil over high heat while stirring

skills.title: Kitchen Safety
skills.explanation: Learn how to stay safe while cooking.
steps: Wash your hands before cooking.
Keep knives pointed down.
Never leave hot pans unattended.
Use oven gloves when handling hot items.
Keep a clean workspace.
skills.tip: Always ask an adult before using the oven or hob.

quiz.question: What should you do before handling food?
Why should you use oven gloves?
options: To protect your hands from heat

skills.title: Knife Skills
skills.explanation: Use a knife safely and effectively.
steps: Choose the right knife for the job.
Use a chopping board.
Curl your fingers under (the 'claw' grip).
Cut slowly and steadily.
Never pass a knife blade-first.
skills.tip: A sharp knife is safer than a blunt one — ask an adult to check.

skills.title: Boiling and Simmering
skills.explanation: Learn to cook with water on the hob.
steps: Fill a pot with cold water and place on the hob.
Turn the heat to high to bring to a boil.
Add food once boiling.
Reduce heat to simmer — small gentle bubbles.
Test food is cooked through before serving.
skills.tip: Salt the water for pasta and vegetables to add flavour.

quiz.question: When do you add pasta to water?

skills.title: Baking Basics
steps: Read the recipe fully before starting.
Measure all ingredients accurately.
Preheat the oven to the correct temperature.
Mix dry and wet ingredients separately then combine.
Test baked goods with a skewer — it should come out clean.
skills.tip: Room-temperature butter creams more easily than cold butter.

quiz.question: Why preheat the oven?
options: So food cooks evenly from the start

quiz.question: How do you test if a cake is baked?
options: Insert a skewer — clean means done

skills.title: Simple Recipes
skills.explanation: Cook three easy meals from scratch.
steps: Scrambled eggs: whisk eggs, cook gently in butter, stir constantly.
Pasta with tomato sauce: boil pasta, fry garlic, add tinned tomatoes, season.
Vegetable stir-fry: chop veg, heat oil, add hard veg first then soft veg, add soy sauce.
skills.tip: Taste as you cook and adjust seasoning gradually.

quiz.question: Which vegetables go into the pan first in a stir-fry?
options: Hard ones like carrot and broccoli

skills.title: Call Emergency Services
skills.description: In an emergency, call your country's emergency number (999 UK, 911 USA, 112 Europe). Say your name, location, and what happened. Stay on the line.

skills.title: Treat a Small Cut
skills.description: Wash hands first. Run cut under clean water. Pat dry. Apply plaster. Tell an adult.

skills.title: Stranger Safety
skills.description: Never go with someone you don't know. Your safe adults are your parents, teachers, and trusted family. If you feel unsafe, go to a crowded place and ask for help.

quiz.question: What is the first thing to do in an emergency?
How do you treat a small cut?
options: Wash with water, dry, and apply a plaster

skills.title: The Recovery Position
skills.description: For an unconscious, breathing person: tilt head back gently, bend closest knee, roll them toward you onto their side, mouth facing down to prevent choking.
skills.why: Prevents choking on vomit in unconscious patients.

skills.title: Treat a Minor Burn
skills.description: Cool with running cold water for at least 10 minutes. Do NOT use ice, butter, or toothpaste. Cover loosely with clean wrap. Seek medical advice for anything larger than a 50p coin.
skills.why: Incorrect burn treatment causes more damage.

skills.title: Respond to Choking
skills.description: If someone is choking and cannot cough, give 5 back blows between shoulder blades. Then 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich manoeuvre). Repeat and call emergency services.
skills.why: Choking can be fatal without immediate action.

quiz.question: How long should you cool a burn with cold water?
What should you NEVER put on a burn?

skills.title: CPR Basics
skills.description: Check for danger, response, airway, breathing. If not breathing normally: 30 chest compressions (push hard and fast, 5–6 cm deep, 100–120 per minute), 2 rescue breaths. Continue until help arrives.
skills.why: CPR can double or triple survival chances after cardiac arrest.

skills.title: Recognise Anaphylaxis
skills.description: Signs: severe rash, swollen throat, difficulty breathing, dizziness. ACTION: Call 999 immediately. If prescribed, help use epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen). Lay person flat, legs raised. Stay until ambulance arrives.
skills.why: Anaphylaxis can be fatal within minutes without treatment.

quiz.question: In CPR, how deep should chest compressions be for an adult?
What is the correct compression rate per minute in CPR?

skills.title: What is First Aid?
skills.explanation: Understand the purpose and limits of first aid.
steps: First aid helps someone who is injured or ill until professional help arrives.
Learn D-R-A-B-C: Danger, Response, Airway, Breathing, Circulation.
Always call emergency services (999 / 112) for serious incidents.
Stay calm so you can help others.
Never put yourself in danger.
skills.tip: D-R-A-B-C is a quick checklist to assess any situation.

quiz.question: What does the 'D' in D-R-A-B-C stand for?
When should you call 999?
options: For any serious illness or injury
Only if you know the person

skills.title: Treating Cuts and Grazes
steps: Wash your hands or use gloves if available.
Rinse the wound under clean running water.
Pat dry gently with a clean cloth.
Apply an antiseptic wipe if available.
Cover with a sterile plaster or bandage.
skills.tip: Do not pick at a scab — it protects the healing skin underneath.

quiz.question: First step when treating a cut?
What should you use to rinse a wound?

skills.title: Burns and Scalds
skills.explanation: Cool a burn and prevent infection.
steps: Cool the burn under cool (not cold/icy) running water for 10–20 minutes.
Do not use butter, oil, or toothpaste.
Remove jewellery near the burn if safe to do so.
Cover loosely with cling film or a clean plastic bag.
Seek medical help for burns larger than a 50p coin.
skills.tip: Never burst blisters — this increases infection risk.

quiz.question: How long should you cool a burn?
What should you NEVER put on a burn?

skills.title: Recovery Position
skills.explanation: Place an unconscious breathing person safely.
steps: Kneel beside the person.
Place the nearest arm at a right angle.
Bring the far hand to rest on the cheek.
Pull up the far knee and roll them towards you.
Tilt the head back to keep the airway open and call 999.
skills.tip: The recovery position prevents an unconscious person from choking on vomit.

quiz.question: Why use the recovery position?
options: To keep the airway open and prevent choking

quiz.question: What should you do after placing someone in recovery position?

skills.title: CPR Basics
skills.explanation: Understand chest compressions and rescue breaths.
steps: Check for danger and response.
Call 999 immediately.
Push down hard and fast on the centre of the chest — 30 compressions.
Give 2 rescue breaths (tilt head, lift chin, seal lips, blow).
Continue 30:2 until help arrives or the person recovers.
skills.tip: Push hard enough — at least 5–6 cm depth on an adult.

quiz.question: CPR compression to breath ratio is?
Where do you place hands for chest compressions?

skills.title: Identify Coins and Notes
skills.description: Learn to identify different coins and notes by their values. Practise counting change. Understand that money is exchanged for goods and services.

skills.title: Save vs Spend
skills.description: Use three jars: Save, Spend, Give. When you receive money, divide it between the jars. The 'Save' jar is for bigger goals.

quiz.question: If you have £1 and spend 40p, how much do you have left?
What is the best habit when you receive money?

skills.title: Budget Your Pocket Money
skills.description: List income (pocket money, gifts). List planned expenses. Subtract expenses from income. If negative, reduce spending. Track actual spending for one month.
skills.why: Budgeting prevents debt and teaches priorities.

skills.title: Needs vs Wants
skills.description: Needs are essentials (food, shelter, clothing). Wants are nice-to-haves (games, sweets, toys). Before buying, ask: 'Is this a need or a want?'
skills.why: Distinguishing needs and wants prevents impulsive spending.

quiz.question: Which of these is a NEED?
If your income is £20 and expenses are £25, what should you do?

skills.title: Understand Compound Interest
skills.description: Compound interest means interest is earned on both the original amount AND previous interest. £100 at 5% per year: Year 1 = £105, Year 2 = £110.25, Year 3 = £115.76. The longer you save, the faster it grows.
skills.why: Understanding compound interest makes you a smarter saver and borrower.

skills.title: Taxes: What and Why
skills.description: Tax is money collected by governments to fund public services (schools, hospitals, roads). Income tax is paid on earnings. VAT is added to goods. Understanding tax helps you plan your finances as an adult.
skills.why: Every citizen needs to understand tax to participate in the economy.

quiz.question: If you invest £1000 at 10% compound interest, what do you have after 2 years?

skills.title: What is Money?
skills.explanation: Understand the purpose and forms of money.
steps: Money is a medium of exchange used to buy goods and services.
Money comes in coins, notes, and digital forms.
Barter (swapping goods directly) existed before money.
Different countries use different currencies.
The value of money can change over time (inflation).
skills.tip: Keep your money safe — only share payment details with trusted adults.

quiz.question: What is a currency?
options: The money used in a country

skills.title: Earning Money
steps: Income is money earned from working.
Wages are paid per hour; salary is a fixed annual amount.
Businesses earn money by selling products or services.
Tax is taken from income to fund public services.
Freelancers are self-employed workers.
skills.tip: Track your pocket money or earnings in a notebook to understand income.

quiz.question: What is income tax used for?

skills.title: Budgeting
skills.explanation: Plan spending to stay within your income.
steps: List all income (money coming in).
List all essential expenses: rent, food, transport.
List optional spending: entertainment, eating out.
Subtract expenses from income to find remaining money.
Adjust spending so you do not spend more than you earn.

quiz.question: A budget is?
options: A plan for how to spend and save money

skills.title: Saving and Interest
skills.explanation: Understand why and how to save money.
steps: Saving means keeping money for future use.
A savings account in a bank earns interest.
Interest is a percentage added to your savings over time.
Compound interest earns interest on interest — money grows faster.
Set a savings goal to stay motivated.
skills.tip: Start saving early — even small amounts grow with compound interest.

quiz.question: Compound interest means?
options: Interest only on the original amount
Interest on both the original amount and previous interest

skills.title: Smart Spending
steps: Distinguish between needs (essentials) and wants (luxuries).
Compare prices before buying — look for value, not just cheapness.
Avoid impulse buying: wait 24 hours before purchasing.
Check return policies before buying.
Use lists when shopping to avoid overspending.
skills.tip: Advertising is designed to make you want things — be a critical consumer.

quiz.question: A 'need' is?
options: Something essential like food or shelter

quiz.question: Best way to avoid impulse buying?

skills.title: Introduction to Scratch
skills.description: Learn what Scratch is and how to navigate the interface.
skills.steps: 1. Open Scratch at scratch.mit.edu. 2. Explore the stage, sprites, and blocks. 3. Drag a 'move 10 steps' block and click it.
skills.activity: Create a sprite that says 'Hello World!' when clicked.

skills.title: Events and Motion
skills.description: Use event blocks to make sprites move.
skills.steps: 1. Use 'when green flag clicked'. 2. Add 'move 10 steps' and 'turn 15 degrees'. 3. Click the green flag.
skills.activity: Make a cat walk across the screen.

skills.title: Loops
skills.description: Use repeat and forever loops.
skills.steps: 1. Use a 'repeat 10' block around motion blocks. 2. Try 'forever' to make continuous motion. 3. Add a wait block inside the loop.
skills.activity: Make a sprite draw a square using a loop.

skills.title: Conditionals
skills.description: Use if-then blocks to make decisions.
skills.steps: 1. Use 'if touching edge then'. 2. Add 'bounce if on edge'. 3. Test with the key pressed sensor.
skills.activity: Create a game where a ball bounces off walls.

skills.title: Variables
skills.description: Store and change values in variables.
skills.steps: 1. Create a variable called 'score'. 2. Set it to 0. 3. Change it by 1 when something happens.
skills.activity: Build a score counter for a simple game.

skills.title: Full Scratch Project
skills.description: Combine all skills to build a complete game.
skills.steps: 1. Design your game. 2. Add sprites, background, score, and lives. 3. Test and debug.
skills.activity: Create a simple platformer or catching game.

quiz.question: Which block starts a Scratch program?

skills.title: Hello World in Python
skills.description: Learn to print output and run Python programs.
skills.why: Python is widely used in science, data, and AI.
skills.steps: 1. Open a Python editor or IDLE. 2. Type print('Hello, World!'). 3. Run the program.
skills.activity: Print your name and age using print().

skills.title: Variables and Data Types
skills.description: Store values in variables and use strings, integers, floats, and booleans.
skills.steps: 1. Create variables: name = 'Ali'; age = 12. 2. Print them. 3. Try arithmetic with numbers.
skills.activity: Create a simple profile printout using variables.

skills.title: User Input
skills.description: Get input from the user using input().
skills.steps: 1. Use name = input('What is your name? '). 2. Print a greeting. 3. Use int(input()) for numbers.
skills.activity: Build a simple calculator using input.

skills.title: Conditionals in Python
skills.description: Use if, elif, else to make decisions.
skills.steps: 1. if age >= 18: print('Adult'). 2. else: print('Child'). 3. Add elif for more options.
skills.activity: Build a number guessing game.

skills.title: Loops in Python
skills.description: Use for and while loops.
skills.steps: 1. for i in range(5): print(i). 2. while count < 10: count += 1. 3. Use break to exit.
skills.activity: Print multiplication tables using a loop.

skills.title: Lists and Dictionaries
skills.description: Store collections of data.
skills.steps: 1. my_list = [1, 2, 3]. 2. my_dict = {'name': 'Ali', 'age': 12}. 3. Access items with indexing.
skills.activity: Build a simple contact book using a dictionary.

skills.title: Functions
skills.description: Define reusable blocks of code.
skills.why: Functions make code modular and reusable.
skills.steps: 1. def greet(name): print('Hello', name). 2. Call it: greet('Ali'). 3. Add return values.
skills.activity: Write functions to calculate area and perimeter.

skills.title: Python Project
skills.description: Build a complete Python project.
skills.steps: 1. Plan: what does your program do? 2. Write the code. 3. Test and debug.
skills.activity: Build a quiz game or to-do list app.

quiz.question: How do you print in Python?

skills.title: Home Row Keys
skills.description: Learn the home row: ASDF JKL;
skills.why: Touch typing is a core modern skill.
skills.steps: 1. Place fingers on ASDF (left) and JKL; (right). 2. Keep fingers on home row. 3. Type without looking.
skills.activity: Type: asdf jkl; asdf jkl; 10 times without looking.

skills.title: Top Row
skills.description: Add QWERTY and UIOP.
skills.steps: 1. Use index fingers to reach Q and U. 2. Practice Q-T and Y-P rows. 3. Return to home row each time.
skills.activity: Type 20 words using top and home rows.

skills.title: Bottom Row
skills.description: Add ZXCV and NM keys.
skills.steps: 1. Reach down with left fingers for ZXCV. 2. Right fingers for NM. 3. Practice without looking.
skills.activity: Type 20 words across all three rows.

skills.title: Speed and Accuracy
skills.description: Build speed to 20+ WPM (words per minute).
skills.steps: 1. Use an online typing game or tutor. 2. Focus on accuracy first. 3. Time yourself for one minute.
skills.activity: Reach 20 WPM with 95% accuracy.

skills.title: Line and Shape
skills.description: Draw basic lines and shapes.
skills.steps: 1. Draw horizontal, vertical, and diagonal lines. 2. Draw circles, squares, and triangles. 3. Combine shapes into a house or robot.
skills.activity: Draw a landscape using only basic shapes.

skills.title: Shading and Tone
skills.description: Add light and dark to create depth.
skills.steps: 1. Draw a circle. 2. Decide where the light comes from. 3. Shade the opposite side using pencil strokes.
skills.activity: Shade a sphere so it looks three-dimensional.

skills.title: Observational Drawing
skills.description: Draw what you see, not what you think.
skills.steps: 1. Place an object (apple, cup) in front of you. 2. Look carefully at the shapes and shadows. 3. Draw slowly and accurately.
skills.activity: Draw a still life of three objects.

skills.title: Perspective
skills.description: Draw objects in one-point perspective.
skills.why: Perspective creates the illusion of depth.
skills.steps: 1. Draw a horizon line and a vanishing point. 2. Draw lines from corners to the vanishing point. 3. Add vertical lines to complete the boxes.
skills.activity: Draw a street receding into the distance.

skills.title: Figure Drawing
skills.description: Draw the human body with correct proportions.
skills.steps: 1. Start with a stick figure 8 heads tall. 2. Add oval shapes for head, torso, limbs. 3. Refine with muscle shapes.
skills.activity: Draw a full standing figure from observation.

quiz.question: A vanishing point is used in:

skills.title: Colour Theory
skills.description: Learn primary, secondary, and complementary colours.
skills.steps: 1. Mix red + blue = purple. 2. Mix yellow + blue = green. 3. Mix red + yellow = orange. 4. Identify complementary pairs.
skills.activity: Paint a colour wheel showing all twelve colours.

skills.title: Brush Techniques
skills.description: Learn different brush strokes and effects.
skills.steps: 1. Try flat washes. 2. Dab for texture. 3. Dry brush for scratchy effects. 4. Wet on wet for soft edges.
skills.activity: Create a painting using at least four different brush techniques.

skills.title: Watercolour Basics
skills.description: Paint with watercolours.
skills.steps: 1. Wet the paper. 2. Apply diluted paint — it spreads. 3. Build up layers when dry. 4. Leave white areas unpainted.
skills.activity: Paint a simple landscape in watercolour.

skills.title: Acrylic Painting
skills.description: Paint with acrylics.
skills.why: Acrylics are versatile and dry quickly.
skills.steps: 1. Apply gesso primer. 2. Sketch your design lightly. 3. Block in large areas first. 4. Add detail last.
skills.activity: Paint a still life in acrylics.

quiz.question: Complementary colours are:
options: colours opposite on the colour wheel

skills.title: Composition
skills.description: Use the rule of thirds and framing.
skills.steps: 1. Imagine a 3x3 grid on your photo. 2. Place subjects on the grid lines. 3. Use natural frames like doorways.
skills.activity: Take 5 photos using the rule of thirds.

skills.title: Light
skills.description: Understand natural and artificial lighting.
skills.why: Light is the most important element in photography.
skills.steps: 1. Shoot facing away from strong light. 2. Use golden hour (just after sunrise / before sunset). 3. Avoid harsh midday shadows.
skills.activity: Take photos at three different times of day.

skills.title: Focus and Depth of Field
skills.description: Choose what is sharp in the photo.
skills.steps: 1. Tap the subject on your phone screen to focus. 2. Portrait mode blurs the background. 3. Landscape mode keeps everything sharp.
skills.activity: Take a portrait with a blurred background.

skills.title: Telling a Story
skills.description: Use a series of photos to tell a story.
skills.steps: 1. Plan: beginning, middle, end. 2. Vary wide, medium, and close-up shots. 3. Include people and action.
skills.activity: Create a photo essay of 8 images on one theme.

quiz.question: The rule of thirds involves:
options: dividing the image into a 3x3 grid

quiz.question: Golden hour is:
options: just after sunrise or before sunset

quiz.question: Depth of field means:
options: how much of the image is in focus

skills.title: Overcoming Nervousness
skills.description: Manage fear of speaking.
skills.steps: 1. Take three slow deep breaths. 2. Remember the audience wants you to succeed. 3. Smile and make eye contact.
skills.activity: Give a 60-second introduction of yourself.

skills.title: Clear Structure
skills.description: Organise your speech.
skills.steps: 1. Plan: introduction, three points, conclusion. 2. Use signpost words: firstly, secondly, finally. 3. Open with a hook.
skills.activity: Prepare and deliver a 2-minute speech on your favourite hobby.

skills.title: Voice and Body Language
skills.description: Use voice, pace, and gestures effectively.
skills.steps: 1. Vary your pace — slow down for important points. 2. Pause for effect. 3. Use open gestures and stand tall.
skills.activity: Record yourself speaking and review your body language.

skills.title: Persuasive Speaking
skills.description: Convince your audience.
skills.steps: 1. State your position clearly. 2. Give three strong reasons with evidence. 3. Address counterarguments. 4. End with a call to action.
skills.activity: Give a 3-minute persuasive speech on a topic you care about.

quiz.question: To overcome nerves before speaking, you should:
Pausing during a speech:
options: adds emphasis and lets ideas sink in

skills.title: Time Management
skills.description: Plan your study time effectively.
skills.steps: 1. List all your tasks. 2. Estimate time for each. 3. Write a weekly schedule. 4. Include breaks.
skills.activity: Create a study schedule for one week.

skills.title: Note-Taking
skills.description: Take useful notes from lessons and reading.
skills.steps: 1. Use headings. 2. Write key points, not everything. 3. Use bullet points and diagrams. 4. Review notes within 24 hours.
skills.activity: Practice the Cornell note-taking method.

skills.title: Active Revision
skills.description: Use active strategies to remember more.
skills.steps: 1. Make flashcards. 2. Test yourself. 3. Teach the topic to someone else. 4. Use past papers.
skills.activity: Create a set of flashcards for one topic.

skills.title: Memory Techniques
skills.description: Use mnemonics, mind maps, and spaced repetition.
skills.steps: 1. Create a mnemonic (e.g. My Very Educated Mother). 2. Draw a mind map. 3. Review material after 1 day, 1 week, 1 month.
skills.activity: Create a mind map of a topic you are studying.

quiz.question: Cornell notes use:
options: headings, key points, and a summary

skills.title: Finding Information
skills.description: Locate reliable information.
skills.why: Research skills are essential for all subjects.
skills.steps: 1. Use search engines with specific keywords. 2. Check the URL — .gov, .edu are usually reliable. 3. Use school databases and libraries.
skills.activity: Find five reliable sources on a topic of your choice.

skills.title: Evaluating Sources
skills.description: Check if a source is trustworthy.
skills.steps: 1. Check the author's credentials. 2. Check the date — is it current? 3. Is the website known and trusted? 4. Does it cite its sources?
skills.activity: Evaluate three websites using the CRAAP test (Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, Purpose).

skills.title: Taking Research Notes
skills.description: Record information without plagiarising.
skills.why: Notes help you organise and use sources.
skills.steps: 1. Read and understand first. 2. Write in your own words. 3. Note the source. 4. Quote only short, important passages.
skills.activity: Take research notes on a topic using three sources.

skills.title: Presenting Research
skills.description: Share your findings clearly.
skills.why: Communicating findings is as important as finding them.
skills.steps: 1. Organise notes into sections. 2. Write an introduction and conclusion. 3. Include a bibliography. 4. Use visual aids.
skills.activity: Present a 5-minute research presentation to your class.

quiz.question: Plagiarism means:
options: using someone else's work without credit

skills.title: Setting Goals
skills.description: Define clear short and long-term goals.
skills.steps: 1. Write SMART goals (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound). 2. Break big goals into small steps. 3. Review progress weekly.
skills.activity: Write one long-term and three short-term goals.

skills.title: Prioritising Tasks
skills.description: Do the most important things first.
skills.steps: 1. List all tasks. 2. Label each A (urgent+important), B (important), C (can wait). 3. Do A tasks first.
skills.activity: Prioritise your tasks for tomorrow using the A-B-C method.

skills.title: Avoiding Procrastination
skills.description: Start tasks without delay.
skills.why: Procrastination wastes time and increases stress.
skills.steps: 1. Start with the hardest task first. 2. Use a 25-minute focus timer (Pomodoro technique). 3. Remove distractions.
skills.activity: Use the Pomodoro technique for one study session.

skills.title: Reflective Review
skills.description: Reflect on how time was used.
skills.steps: 1. At the end of each day, review what you did. 2. Celebrate what you achieved. 3. Adjust tomorrow's plan.
skills.activity: Keep a time log for one school day.

skills.title: Planting Seeds
skills.description: Sow seeds correctly.
skills.steps: 1. Fill a pot with compost. 2. Make a small hole. 3. Place the seed and cover. 4. Water gently. 5. Place in sunlight.
skills.activity: Plant five seeds and record their growth over two weeks.

skills.title: Plant Care
skills.description: Water, feed, and look after plants.
skills.steps: 1. Check soil moisture before watering. 2. Give liquid feed once a week. 3. Remove dead leaves. 4. Protect from frost.
skills.activity: Care for a pot plant for one month, recording your actions.

skills.title: Growing Vegetables
skills.description: Grow edible plants.
skills.why: Growing food is rewarding and sustainable.
skills.steps: 1. Choose easy vegetables: tomatoes, lettuce, radish, beans. 2. Prepare soil or a container. 3. Plant, water, and harvest.
skills.activity: Grow a vegetable from seed to harvest.

skills.title: Composting
skills.description: Make compost from food waste.
skills.why: Composting reduces waste and enriches soil.
skills.steps: 1. Collect vegetable peel, eggshells, and garden waste. 2. Layer green (wet) and brown (dry) material. 3. Turn weekly. 4. Use after 2-3 months.
skills.activity: Start a compost bin or bucket.

quiz.question: Why is composting good?
options: it reduces waste and makes rich soil

quiz.question: Before watering, you should:
options: check if the soil is already moist

skills.title: Setting Up the Board
skills.description: Learn the pieces and their starting positions.
skills.steps: 1. The board has 64 squares. 2. Place pieces: rooks in corners, knights next, bishops, then queen on her colour, king. 3. Pawns fill the second row.
skills.activity: Set up a chess board correctly five times.

skills.title: How Pieces Move
skills.description: Learn the moves of each piece.
skills.steps: 1. Pawns move forward, capture diagonally. 2. Rooks move in straight lines. 3. Bishops move diagonally. 4. Knights move in an L-shape. 5. Queens can move in any direction. 6. Kings move one square any direction.
skills.activity: Play a game where each player uses only one type of piece.

skills.title: Check and Checkmate
skills.description: Understand the goal of chess.
skills.steps: 1. Check: the king is under attack. 2. The king must escape check. 3. Checkmate: the king cannot escape — the game ends.
skills.activity: Set up and solve five checkmate puzzles.

skills.title: Basic Strategy
skills.description: Plan your game.
skills.why: Strategy makes you a better player.
skills.steps: 1. Control the centre. 2. Develop your pieces early. 3. Protect your king by castling. 4. Do not give pieces away for nothing.
skills.activity: Play five complete games applying basic strategy.

skills.title: Warm-Up Routine
skills.description: Prepare the body for exercise.
skills.steps: 1. March in place for 2 minutes. 2. Do 10 arm circles each way. 3. Do 10 leg swings each leg. 4. Jog in place for 1 minute.
skills.activity: Complete a 5-minute warm-up before any exercise session.

skills.title: Cardiovascular Exercise
skills.description: Strengthen the heart and lungs.
skills.steps: 1. Try running, jumping jacks, cycling, or swimming. 2. Aim for 20–30 minutes. 3. Keep a pace where you can speak but are breathing harder.
skills.activity: Do 20 minutes of cardio exercise three times this week.

skills.title: Strength Training
skills.description: Build muscle using body weight.
skills.steps: 1. Try push-ups, squats, lunges, and sit-ups. 2. Aim for 3 sets of 10 reps each. 3. Rest 60 seconds between sets.
skills.activity: Complete a beginner body-weight workout.

skills.title: Flexibility and Stretching
skills.description: Stretch safely to improve range of motion.
skills.steps: 1. Hold each stretch 20–30 seconds. 2. Never bounce a stretch. 3. Target hamstrings, quads, shoulders, and back.
skills.activity: Complete a 10-minute stretching routine after exercise.

skills.title: Creating a Fitness Plan
skills.description: Design a balanced weekly exercise plan.
skills.steps: 1. Aim for 60 minutes of activity daily. 2. Include cardio, strength, and flexibility. 3. Rest is also important — include 1–2 rest days.
skills.activity: Design and follow a 2-week fitness plan.

quiz.question: How long should you hold a stretch?

skills.title: Breathing Exercises
skills.description: Learn controlled breathing.
skills.why: Breathing calms the mind and body.
skills.steps: 1. Sit comfortably. 2. Breathe in for 4 counts. 3. Hold for 4. 4. Breathe out for 4. 5. Repeat 5 times.
skills.activity: Practice 4-4-4 breathing for 5 minutes.

skills.title: Basic Yoga Poses
skills.description: Learn five foundational poses.
skills.steps: 1. Mountain pose: stand tall, arms by sides. 2. Tree pose: balance on one leg. 3. Downward dog. 4. Child's pose. 5. Warrior I.
skills.activity: Hold each of the five poses for 30 seconds.

skills.title: Mindfulness Meditation
skills.description: Focus on the present moment.
skills.steps: 1. Sit comfortably. 2. Close your eyes. 3. Focus on your breath. 4. When your mind wanders, gently bring it back. 5. Practise for 5 minutes.
skills.activity: Practice mindfulness for 5 minutes daily for one week.

skills.title: Body Scan Relaxation
skills.description: Release tension from the body.
skills.steps: 1. Lie down. 2. Close your eyes. 3. Mentally scan from toes to head. 4. Release tension in each body part. 5. Breathe slowly throughout.
skills.activity: Complete a full body scan relaxation.

skills.title: Basic Folds
skills.description: Learn valley fold and mountain fold.
skills.why: Origami develops concentration and fine motor skills.
skills.steps: 1. Valley fold: fold paper up towards you. 2. Mountain fold: fold paper away from you. 3. Practice both on a square sheet.
skills.activity: Make 10 valley folds and 10 mountain folds accurately.

skills.title: Simple Models
skills.description: Fold a paper crane and boat.
skills.steps: 1. Start with a square. 2. Fold diagonally twice. 3. Open and collapse to a smaller square. 4. Follow crane steps.
skills.activity: Fold a traditional paper crane.

skills.title: Modular Origami
skills.description: Create models from multiple units.
skills.steps: 1. Fold six identical units. 2. Assemble them into a cube or star. 3. Each unit locks into the next.
skills.activity: Create a six-unit modular cube.

skills.title: Threading a Needle
skills.description: Learn to thread a needle safely.
skills.why: Sewing is a practical life skill.
skills.steps: 1. Cut a 50cm length of thread. 2. Wet the end slightly. 3. Pass through the needle eye. 4. Knot the end.
skills.activity: Thread a needle and knot the thread five times.

skills.title: Running Stitch
skills.description: Sew a basic running stitch.
skills.why: Running stitch is the foundation of sewing.
skills.steps: 1. Mark your stitch line. 2. Push needle up through fabric. 3. Push down then up again. 4. Keep stitches even.
skills.activity: Sew a running stitch in a straight line and a curve.

skills.title: Sewing a Simple Project
skills.description: Sew a small pouch or bookmark.
skills.steps: 1. Cut two rectangles. 2. Sew three sides using running stitch. 3. Turn inside out. 4. Fill and sew the opening.
skills.activity: Sew a small fabric pouch.

skills.title: Basic Knitting or Crochet
skills.description: Learn to cast on and knit, or crochet a chain.
skills.steps: 1. Cast on 10 stitches. 2. Knit 10 rows. 3. Cast off. OR 1. Hold hook and yarn. 2. Create a slip knot. 3. Chain 20 stitches.
skills.activity: Complete a small knitted or crocheted swatch.

quiz.question: A running stitch:
options: is a basic hand stitch in and out

quiz.question: Why should you knot thread?
options: to stop it pulling through the fabric

quiz.question: Casting on in knitting means:
options: starting with stitches on the needle
